newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates up on bids by finance firms.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates up on bids by finance firms.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates were slightly firmer on Wednesday, boosted by bids by finance companies seeking fresh funds, dealers said.
"Finance houses are bidding up rates. A couple of big banks are also believed to be short of funds," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the longer-term rates were largely neglected.

Dealers said they expected rates to hold although there will be a maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday. They expect the central bank to call for a fresh Bank Negara bill issue next week.

Dealers said there was a persistent rumour about a possible long-term government bond issue soon, which would mop up liquidity and roll over maturing bonds. A 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue will mature on May 15.
One-week money was unchanged at 6.8/7.0 percent, two-week at 7.10/20 percent against 7.00/10 on Tuesday and three-week at 7.20/25 percent from 7.10/20.
One-month money at 7.25/30 percent, three-month at 7.30/35 and six-month at 7.35/40, were all unchanged.
The overnight interbank rate is expected to remain between 6.5 and 7.0 percent, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange fell back after gains on Tuesday.
At 0300 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down two points to 92.67, or an implied yield of 7.33 percent.
December and March 1998 were down one each to 92.67 and 92.60, or 7.33 and 7.40 percent respectively.
